title: Payment allocation: synthetic software breakdown
question: What can this tiny payment fixture establish, and what would a real system still need?
summary: The original fixture keeps applied payment, remaining invoice balance and unapplied funds separate. This example demonstrates evidence-linked reporting, not a production payment integration.

sources.title: Original payment.mjs fixture and four executable assertions
sources.scope: One original function; partial payment, overpayment, negative input and fractional input assertions ran through Node.
sources.limitations: No processor, database, concurrent request, tax or invoice lifecycle is implemented.

sources.title: REA static JavaScript analysis of examples directory
sources.scope: Inert syntax inspection through the actual REA CLI.
sources.limitations: Static analysis does not execute the function or establish production behavior; full raw output is generated locally and not redistributed.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: A partial payment of 3000 against a balance of 10000 leaves 7000 remaining and no unapplied funds.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: A payment of 15000 against a balance of 10000 applies 10000 and retains 5000 unapplied.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: The fixture rejects negative or fractional minor-unit values in the executed assertions.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: REA returned a structured static-analysis evidence envelope for the examples directory.
findings.caveat: This establishes a real inspection ran, not that REA proved every business rule or any production workflow.

requirements.text: Preserve received, allocated and unapplied amounts separately.
requirements.acceptance: Partial and overpayment cases retain the original amounts and reconcile the allocation totals.

requirements.text: Define duplicate-effect and reconciliation behavior before connecting a payment provider.
requirements.acceptance: A provider timeout and repeated notification do not create duplicate money movement; durable provider readback resolves uncertainty.

unknowns: Provider authorization, capture, settlement, refund and dispute handling.
Persistent allocation records, concurrent updates, client isolation and audit history.
Jurisdiction-specific tax, accounting and payment obligations.
Human review is still required to assess whether findings are supported by their sources.
